properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-14: "as we designed reflow2/flo2 to be the partnership between human + AI + graph (reflow2), I feel that reflow2 now becomes the way for an AI model to write down/transcribe its "reasoning" process into a graphical representation. So often, humans are skeptical of AI because we can't really see how AI arrived at something. We still have a hard time arriving at this, but at least with reflow2, the AI agent can put down its thought process in something that can be critically analyzed. I think this probably lines up with a lot of things already in the reflow2 design".

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED. He is right that most of it is on the record:
- dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well, the few jobs (2026-10-13):
  - Job 1: "Keep one shared record of what was decided, by whom and why, across every model, person and agent."
  - Job 3: "checks that don't reason and can't be talked round".
  - Job 5: "you can see what the agent filled in".
  - Why jobs 1 and 3 changed: "a model's judgement is not a check", and vendor memory "is not auditable".
- req:the-site-says-what-reflow2-is-and-is-not-as-a-partnership-in-plain-words (accepted): "a person decides, an AI drafts, asks and checks, and a graph remembers".
- dec:idea-what-did-the-agent-infer-provenance-per-field-per-type-and-as-a-report (settled 2026-10-13): what the person said is shown apart from what the agent filled in.
- req:a-write-and-an-approval-record-the-agent-and-the-person-it-acts-for (accepted): every write names the agent and the person.
- Tonight's A, B, C and E (accepted) give the "why" a STRUCTURE: premises, a rule, a conclusion, who confirmed it, and the axioms underneath.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and only this: today an agent's "why" is a RATIONALE PARAGRAPH, which a person can read but no check can test. Once C exists, should an agent's CONSEQUENTIAL recommendation be recorded as an inference chain instead, so each step can be challenged, checked for form and confirmed?

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) SERVED INSTRUCTIONS ASK FOR IT on consequential recommendations (a decision the person will act on, a cause written down), and leave everything else as prose.
(b) A READ THAT TURNS A RATIONALE INTO A PROPOSED CHAIN for the person to confirm, so the agent's argument is checked before it is relied on.
(c) NOTHING NEW. A, B, C and E make it possible, and agents use it when it helps.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- WHAT A MODEL WRITES DOWN IS ITS STATED ARGUMENT, NOT ITS INTERNAL PROCESS. Research on the faithfulness of model explanations has found that a model's written reasoning can differ from what actually drove its answer. So reflow2 makes AI reasoning CHECKABLE, not TRANSPARENT. That is still the right thing: mathematics settled long ago that you trust a proof by checking it, not by seeing inside the prover's head. The claim to make is "every step can be checked on its merits", never "this is how the AI thought".
- CEREMONY: a chain for every remark would bury the ones that matter. Hence "consequential" in (a).
- STRUCTURE IS NOT TRUTH (job 3): a well-formed chain with a false premise passes the form check. The value is that the false premise is now a node someone can point at.

SIZE (a finding): (a) is small, served text, once C exists. (b) is moderate. (c) is nothing.
